key:
"Delve deep into the forgotten ruins of the once great Dwarven Halls. Adventure into the untamed wilds of the Emerald Jungle. Uncover the mysteries of the Sunken Swamplands.  Face all new foes: creeping spiders, giant scorpions, Great Wyrms and more.

We’re excited for you to try out our new areas as well as revamped versions of all our  existing areas. There will no longer be any loading between traveling and battling – everything will take place on our new world maps. We hope you enjoy this seamless experience which offers a much greater variety of strategic battling locations and delightful areas to explore.


[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added 3 new environments (Swamp, Dwarven Halls, and Jungle) each with new enemies to fight
[*] There is no longer a transition teleporting you from the world map to the battle – instead you fight the battle directly on the world map
[*] The rooms that are spawned in after activating a navigation node are now randomly generated, look better atheistically and able to support battling directly in the room
[*] Added 4 new boss fights: Olgoi the Devourer of Treasure, The Witch, The Council and Medusa
[*] Added 10 new Fortunes: Silver Signet, Emblem of the Iron Fortress, Elixir of the Scarlet Ox, Frozen Lich Heart, Scroll of Monster Summoning, Touch of Frost, Touch of Thunder, Elemental Mastery, Rune of Refreshment, and Ball Lightning
[*] Added new items
[*] Possible movement and action hexes are now displayed using a border instead of highlighting every hex to reduce visual clutter
[*] Added language support for Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, and French
[*] Added line of sight indicators
[*] Important objects obstructed from view now highlight through their obstructions
[*] Fishing now occurs at bodies of water that naturally spawn in the world
[*] Added a new shop feature that can upgrade any item to your current level for gold.
[*] You can now right click a Fortune to unequip it
[*] Various performance optimizations
[/list]

[h2]General Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] The quest selection map is now non-linear to where you can decide what environment you travel to 
[*] There is now a ‘'placement phase' before battle where you can arrange your party's starting positions
[*] There is now only one activation hex that opens in the next area in the world map which brings up a menu with the various room options.
[*] The party now votes for which room to open up next
[*] ’Teleporting’ enemy modifier can now only trigger once per turn
[*] ’Regenerating’ enemy modifier is no longer based on a percentage of max health but is instead a flat amount based on level
[*] ’Rampaging’ now gives the enemy the ability to rampage after control effects are used instead of always being Rampaged.  Also it no longer grants extra movement.
[*] Greatly increased the health per level player summons receive
[*] Changed visual effect for Light’s Beckon
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed some issues where objects would block line of sight when they shouldn’t
[*] Fixed issue where Soul Link wouldn’t function on a killing blow
[*] Fixed issue with Enrage refreshing duration when movement impairing effects are used on an enemy that is already enraged
[*] Fixed issue with the game not properly loading if you click the Continue button multiple times
[*] Fixed issue where you couldn’t access the pause menu while in an event
[/list]
"

[h2][b]TURN-BASED STRATEGY MEETS ACTION RPG IN THIS DUNGEON CRAWLING LOOTER[/b][/h2]


Stolen Realm is a [b]simultaneous turn-based tactical dungeon crawling looter with action RPG elements[/b] where you control up to [b]6 heroes, solo or through online co-op[/b], venturing forth in adventures set in a high-fantasy, low-poly world. 

Stolen Realm features an [b]innovative turn-based combat system[/b] where [b]simultaneous turns[/b] allow every team to take their actions at once, creating quick combat encounters that blend the tactical depth of titles like Divinity: Original Sin with the thrill of a fast-paced action RPG. Every battle scales based on the number of players involved, so you can easily jump in and out of the game even in the same playthrough!
 
With a [b]highly customisable class system[/b], Stolen Realm allows you to create traditional RPG classes or break the mold to forge a unique champion of your own as you draw from a pool of hundreds of possible skills. Make a spell-slinging assassin, a priest born of frost, or a shadow-infused knight. Further customize your build by earning and reforging [b]loot that truly changes the way you play[/b]: wield Abbadon the Soul Crusher, a mythic mace that raises slain enemies as skeletal warriors to fight for you, or unsheath the Bloodletter, a cursed sword that grants additional power at the cost of your lifeblood. D&D-like events where attribute-based rolls will have permanent effects on your character add yet another layer to building a character that is truly your own. Anything is possible in this title that keeps compelling choices at the forefront of your experience.  

Keeping the core appeal of RPGs at its forefront, Stolen Realm ensures you spend all your time, fighting, building your characters and making compelling choices that determine your immediate path or effect your character, rather than getting bogged down in side quests and other RPG-bloat.   After each battle, pick your path between story events, resource gathering, shops and treasure rooms, until you get to the final boss of each [b]procedurally generated adventure.[/b] If you’re up to a challenge, crank the difficulty up with [b]6 different difficulty levels[/b] – or pick [b]Hardcore Mode with permadeath[/b], where every battle can be the last!

Carve a place in history with your sword and magic. Rise to honor and glory in the battlefield. [b]Recover the Stolen Realm.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_APP_IMAGE}/extras/dragon.gif[/img]

[h2]PRAISE FOR STOLEN REALM[/h2]


“You can be a fire warrior. You can be a healing necromancer. You can do all sorts of weird s**t.” - [b]Sacriel[/b]

“What I like about this game is it’s straight to the point. You just go in, you’re building your character, you’re getting items…and you just fight. There’s no bulls**t.” - [b]Shroud[/b]

“It’s rad” - [b]Sequisha[/b]


[img]{STEAM_APP_IMAGE}/extras/characters.gif[/img]


[h2][b]KEY FEATURES[/b][/h2]


[list][*]Play solo or with friends in up to 6 player online co-op, allowing you and your friends to wreak havoc amongst your foes
[*]Experience thrilling and fast-paced turn-based battles thanks to a simultaneous team turn system
[*]Use over 300 skills in 9 distinct skill trees allowing for complete and flexible character customization
[*]Navigate hex-based battlefields where positioning is key due to battle shrines with special effects, exploding barrels and movable crates
[*]Find and loot over 700 unique items, fully customizable with modifiers, as you explore a wonderful world full of magic, secrets and unexpected dangers
[*]Co-op focused design keeps gameplay fast paced and strategic for up to 6 players 
[*]Easy drop-in, drop-out design and automatic scaling that allows you to join or drop out mid-quest 
[*]D&D-like attribute-based rolls in special events that have permanent character effects
[*]Fight against over 200 types of enemies in battles that will be different every time: thanks to the Enemy Modifications feature, every creature you face on the battlefield will be unique
[*]A world that changes on each expedition, from frosty peaks guarded by the elusive Blue Dragon to overgrown jungles where the rock giants roam. 
[*]Pick your path between battles, choosing where to go between story events, resource gathering, shops, fights, and treasure rooms until you get to the final boss of each adventure
[*]6 different difficulty levels
[*]Choose between Normal Mode and Hardcore Mode with permadeath if you want a real challenge![/list]

As you draw near the dwarven throne, a profound melancholy envelops Ironheart. "Long ago," the king began, his voice echoing off the cold stone walls, "our halls shone with the light of a thousand torches, and our forges burned bright, crafting wonders the likes of which the world has never seen since. And now?" the Mountain King jestures dismally at the surrounding ruins. "Long have the dragons slumbered," his voice rumbles, deep as the earth, "but we paid dearly for it." "A tempest of fire and fury they were. In our desperation, we turned to forbidden powers, dark powers..." He pauses, his gaze distant, haunted. "We tried, lad. You can't say we didn't try."
With sudden intensity, his eyes, like smoldering coals, fix on you. "Your father, he had an insatiable curiosity, always delving where eyes shouldn't pry. He dug too deep, too greedily in my kingdom." A madness dances in the Mountain King's eyes, the flickering flames of a once-noble spirit now consumed by fear and desperation. "I sent them, the bandits, to protect what is mine. But you persisted, like your father. And now, you leave me no choice. I cannot allow you or your father's legacy to leave these halls. The secrets of my kingdom must remain within these walls, even if it means your end."

key:
In a final, catastrophic moment, volatile energies tear through the Sultan, reducing him to nothing but ash. From the remnants of the Sultan's demise, a faint light begins to emerge, growing brighter and more tangible. Out of the ashes floats an amulet, its gold shimmering with an ethereal light, untouched by the destruction that had just unfolded. The moment your fingers touch the necklace, a rush of energy surges through you, and you are transported once more into a vivid memory that is not your own.
You find yourself witnessing a moment of profound intimacy and love – the Sultan, a man now unrecognizable from the tyrant you had just faced, in a tender embrace with a beautiful woman with raven-black hair. The Sultan's expression, devoid of the hardness and cruelty that had marked his face in battle, is filled with genuine affection and happiness. The couple seem utterly at peace, lost in their love for each other.
As quickly as it had begun, the vision dissipates, leaving you standing in the blinding heat of Wyrmrest. With the amulet now in your possession, you turn your attention back to the path laid out in your father's journal. It beckons you onwards, towards the vast and treacherous expanse of the sea.

key:
In the moment of her defeat, as if by some ancient and unfathomable magic, the Medusa turns to stone. Her form, forever captured in a tableau of anguish and rage, becomes a statue, a permanent testament to her tragic fate. The jungle around you falls into an eerie silence, as if the very earth and sky are pausing to mourn the loss of this creature as cursed as she was fearsome. And then a light emanates, growing in intensity, from within the statue. A jewel, brilliant and green, appears, its facets exquisitely wrought, as if by the hands of a master artisan.
You take the jewel and see a woman, strong and fierce, her eyes alight with the fire of leadership and the warmth of compassion. She sits upon a throne, not as a tyrant ruling with an iron fist, but as a chieftain who leads her people with care and protection. Her presence is commanding, yet there is a kindness in her demeanor, a love for her people that is palpable. Her people look to her with respect and affection. She does not stand above them, but among them, a leader who bares the responsibility of her position not as a burden, but as a sacred duty.
The vision fades, leaving you once again in the heart of the jungle, the stone form of the Medusa before you. The curse that plagues this realm, turning its protectors into monsters and its beauty into peril, is a blight that you are determined to end.

key:
In the stark silence of Frostwrought Mountain's summit, the skeletal form of the Dusk King lay defeated. The once-mighty lich, now nothing more than bones scattered in the snow. From the fallen form of the Dusk King, a light begins to emerge, piercing the gloom of the mountain. It emanates from the king's armor, revealing a crown of pure gold, its jewels gleaming with an inner light. As your fingers grasp the crown, a vision envelopes you, transporting you to a time and place far removed from this icy desolation.
You are in a grand hall, resplendent with banners and the warm glow of torchlight. Before you stands a noble king, regal and benevolent, his eyes shining with pride. The king is bestowing a great honor upon a young warrior, who kneels before him in humble reverence. Through the eyes of the vision, you feel the overwhelming joy of a proud parent, the king witnessing his own son receiving the honor of knighthood.
The vision fades, leaving you once again on the frozen summit, staring at the lifeless form of the Dusk King. Your father had indeed discovered that the cure the ancient kings had sought for the dragons had imparted a terrible curse – a solution that had brought untold suffering and transformed protectors into tormented guardians of a dark legacy. The need to find your father is more pressing than ever.

key:
Shadowy chains, manifestations of the curse that had consumed Blackbeard's soul, emerge from the abyss, reaching for the fallen pirate. With an inexorable grip, they pull him down into the unfathomable depths of darkness, an abyss where greed and power has led him. A soft glow emanates from the spot where Blackbeard had vanished. There, lying amidst the ancient stones of the temple, is a brilliant gold coin, radiant and untouched by the darkness that had just been vanquished. Tentatively, you reach out and touch the coin, its surface cool and smooth under your fingers.
You are carried aboard a ship, the deck alive with the sounds of the sea – the creaking of wood, the cry of gulls, and the rush of the wind. Here, amidst the salt and spray, sits a young Blackbeard, his face unmarked by the years of hardship and cruelty that would later define him. His hair is tousled by the sea breeze, and his eyes sparkle with the untamed spirit of adventure. The young Blackbeard is laughing heartily, surrounded by his shipmates, as they engage in a game of chance. The atmosphere is light and jovial, filled with the camaraderie of men and women who share a love for the sea and the thrill of adventure. They are brothers in arms, united by the bonds forged in the vast and unpredictable embrace of the ocean.
Your mind is awash with questions, a torrent as tumultuous as the sea that surrounds the ruins. The memories unveiled by these magical artifacts paints pictures of lives that had once been, lives of men before they were consumed by the shadows of their desires. You can't help but ponder the enigma your father is unraveling, a mystery that intertwines the fates of these men with the ancient and mysterious defeat of the dragons. The journal now points towards a new destination – the frosty peaks of Frostwrought Mountain.

key:
The Witch's form, once a vessel of corruption and malevolence, begins to dissolve. Her cruel visage, twisted by years of darkness, bubbles and melts into the swamp itself, as if the land is reclaiming a part of its lost self. The foul air and the murky waters around her seeth and churn, swallowing the remnants of her existence. From the dissipating form of the Witch, a light rises, pure and cleansing. It swirls amidst the foul miasma of the swamp, a beacon of hope in the heart of despair. Encased within this light is a simple object, starkly out of place in the grim surroundings – a child's teddy bear, worn by time but still holding the echoes of innocence and care. You reach out and take the bear. As your fingers brush against its fabric, a vision envelopes you, transporting you to a time and place far removed from the decay of the swamp.
You find yourself in a forest at night, a world away from the corruption you have just witnessed. Above, the stars shine brightly, their light filtering through the canopy to dance upon the forest floor. The air is alive with the sound of crickets and the gentle movement of fireflies, a symphony of the night. There, in a clearing, lays a young girl, the Witch in her innocent youth, curled up beside her pet wolf. Both sleep peacefully, nestled together for warmth under the starlit sky. The girl, a caretaker of the forest, is at home in this natural haven, her heart intertwined with the life around her. The vision is a glimpse into a past untainted by darkness, a time of innocence and harmony.
As the vision fades, you are brought back to the grim reality of the Sunken Swamp. The beautiful forest of the vision is now the stinking bog that surrounds you, a bleak reminder of the transformation wrought by the curse. With the child's bear in hand, the final relic mentioned in your father's journal, you know that your quest is nearing its end. You have gathered the artifacts, each a key to understanding the depth of the curse that had befallen the realm. Now, all that remains is to retrace the last steps of your father, to follow the path that would lead him to the looming Castle Gloom.

key:
The remaining Blood Masks, witnessing the defeat of their leader, succumb to their cowardly nature. They scatter, fleeing into the shadows of the forest.
Amongst their stolen plunder, you unearth your Father's leather-bound journal. Worn with age, it contains a lifetimes worth of knowledge, gained from his countless adventures across the realm. Memories flood your mind as you recall your final moments with him. As you stand there, thumbing through the journal, a pit of worry gnaws at your stomach. Your father would not have parted with this, his life's work, willingly, nor in sound mind.
If what the bandit said was true, then the old Mountain King Ironheart might hold clues to your father's disappearance. The journey to Ironheart would be a perilous path through the Forgotten Mines, veering into the remnants of a once-glorious dwarven realm. There, amidst the echoes of a bygone era, the dwarf king reigned over a kingdom fractured, its splendor lost to the corridors of time. The thought of this distant land and untold tales, stirs within your heart the beginnings of another adventure.

key:
The summit is a desolate expanse, a frozen wasteland where the wind howls with the cries of lost souls. Here, amidst the eternal snows and beneath the grey, brooding sky, you are confronted by a figure as chilling as the frostbitten air itself - the Dusk King, an undead lich whose very presence exudes an aura of bitter cold that seems to leach the warmth from the world.
His voice is like the rustling of dead leaves, a sound both haunting and ageless. "You tread the path your father once walked, seeking to unravel the tapestries of fate we have woven. But you cannot fathom the choices we were forced to make, the sacrifices we bore to keep the dragons at bay." "The Dead One feeds upon the dragons, eating their minds, driving them into a slumber from which they can not awaken."
"Should you, or your father, undo the bindings that we have wrought to hold the dragons at bay, it would unleash a cataclysm upon the world." "I cannot permit the world to fall into such peril again." the lich declares, his voice resolute in its somber decree.
With those ominous words, the snow around you begins to stir, as if responding to the will of the Dusk King. From the white expanse emerge figures, ghastly and gruesome, the undead who lay frozen beneath the frost.

key:
With a final, mighty blow you strike down the mighty dwarf. The madness in Ironheart's eyes fade, and for a moment, he is the noble king he once was. Suddenly, from the depths of his armor, a soft glow begins to emerge. It's a light so pure and gentle, it seems out of place in the dark, cold hall. A small feather, illuminated in a halo of light, floats gracefully from his chest. It's a robin's feather, delicate and beautiful, a symbol of life and new beginnings. Compelled by an unknown force, you reach out and grasp the feather. The moment your fingers touch it, the world around you dissolves. You are enveloped in a memory so vivid, it's as though you've been transported through time.
You find yourself in the dwarven halls of restored splendor, one filled with warmth and laughter. Before you sits Ironheart, but not as the deranged monarch you had just battled. This is Ironheart in his youth, a robust and cheerful king, his eyes sparkling with joy and kindness. On his lap, giggling with innocent delight, is a small dwarven child, his daughter. She playfully tugs at his beard, her laughter echoing through the hall, a sound of pure happiness.
As the memory fades you find yourself back in the present, with the magical feather still warm in your hand. For a long moment, you stare at it, recalling your reading about this very feather in your father's journal. You had dismissed it as a figment of your father's illness-induced imagination, a fanciful creation borne from the erratic and fragmented later entries of the journal. But now, as the feather lay tangible and radiant in your hand, the reality of its existence shakes your understanding of what is possible. Chronicled within the journal is not only this feather but also other items of mystical importance scattered across the realm. The next item of importance, as described in the journal, is an amulet, said to be in the possession of a sultan in the deserts of Wyrmrest.

key:
The summit is a desolate expanse, a frozen wasteland where the wind howls with the cries of lost souls. Here, amidst the eternal snows and beneath the grey, brooding sky, you are confronted by a figure as chilling as the frostbitten air itself - the Dusk King, an undead lich whose very presence exudes an aura of bitter cold that seems to leach the warmth from the world.
His voice is like the rustling of dead leaves, a sound both haunting and ageless. "You tread the path your father once walked, seeking to unravel the tapestries of fate we have woven. But you cannot fathom the choices we were forced to make, the sacrifices we bore to keep the dragons at bay." "The Dead One feeds upon the dragons, eating their minds, driving them into a slumber from which they can not awaken."
"Should you, or your father, undo the bindings that we have wrought to hold the dragons at bay, it would unleash a cataclysm upon the world." "I cannot permit the world to fall into such peril again." the lich declares, his voice resolute in its somber decree.
With those ominous words, the snow around you begins to stir, as if responding to the will of the Dusk King. From the white expanse emerge figures, ghastly and gruesome, the undead who lay frozen beneath the frost.

key:

"Good eve," he rasps, his voice like gravel and smoke. "Are you in need of sustenance?"

The man extends a gnarled hand, presenting a trio of dishes, each more horrifying than the last.

First, a bubbling, steaming cauldron of a soup, its murky surface breaking to reveal human hands, fingers curled as though grasping for escape. Next, a plate of what seems to be oversized cockroaches, their bodies crisp and their wings crackling as if recently deep-fried. And finally, a platter bearing a single, massive, dark purple tentacle. It twitches, even in its cooked state, muscles rippling under its suckered skin, making the dish appear as though it was still alive.
